chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from the one who narrated to him, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Abī 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
It is appropriate for the Imam to remain at Jam' until the sun rises, while the rest of the people, if they wish, may hasten, and if they wish, may delay.
So the proper understanding of this report is the removal of hardship from whoever does that, and the first two reports are to be understood as indicating a kind of recommendation.

key_terms.أَخَّرُوا: they delayed; meaning they remained longer before departing
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; a non-obligatory but preferred legal ruling
key_terms.بِجَمْعٍ: at Jam'; the sacred site of Muzdalifah referred to in the hajj rites
key_terms.رَفْعُ الْحَرَجِ: removal of hardship; indicating legal concession and absence of undue restriction
key_terms.عَجَّلُوا: they hastened; meaning they departed earlier
key_terms.لِلْإِمَامِ: for the Imam; the leader whose practice sets the principal standard here

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory to remain at Jam' until sunrise, or is it only recommended?
ai.summary: This report concerns the recommended time of departing from Jam' during hajj rites. It indicates that the Imam should remain until sunrise, while others are given leeway to leave earlier or later, and it reconciles prior reports by interpreting them as expressing recommendation rather than obligation.
